content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] [version_no]. I would like to know if it's possible to use one output for running a 220V device and another output for running a 24V device. Does anyone know if this is possible?
Hi, the 'R' in the name of [product_name] indicates relay outputs. Each relay can be wired with a different voltage. Please refer to the manual for more details.

Yes, you can use an output for another voltage, but make sure your [product_name] has the 'R' version. In the manual, look at the section about connecting outputs, which shows how to wire different voltages to outputs.

Hello! The [product_name] [version_no] modules have isolated relay outputs. The program only closes the relay; you can supply one side of a relay with 220V AC, and when closed, it connects to your circuit. Similarly, you can connect 12V DC to another relay output and provide it to a different circuit. This applies to all relay outputs, even expansion modules (with a 5A current limit). The main unit relays can handle up to 10A AC, but for DC current, it's advised not to exceed 8A for increased relay lifespan. Have a great day!
Thank you all, your input was very helpful.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants discussed how the [product_name] module allows for switching devices with different voltages using individual relay outputs, due to their isolated design. While there was initial uncertainty, experienced members clarified the wiring options and advised consulting the manual for correct setup and current limitations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to connect devices with different voltages to separate outputs of a [product_name] module securely and reliably, without being constrained by hardware design.
